title: docs: add blocking and long-running work section to WebSockets

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Documentation about how to use FastAPI

body:
## Description

The WebSockets page doesn't mention that WebSocket handlers are always `async def`: unlike *path operation functions*, there's no plain `def` option where FastAPI runs the function in an external threadpool. Because of this, users coming from HTTP endpoints naturally assume the same `def`-threadpool escape hatch exists, run blocking code in a WebSocket handler, and freeze every other connection in the app.

This is a recurring confusion point (see the discussions on running long CPU-bound tasks without dropping WebSocket connections) and it is currently covered nowhere: `async.md` explains the threadpool mechanism for `def` *path operation functions* but never mentions WebSockets, and `advanced/websockets.md` never mentions blocking code or the event loop.

Adds a short section to the WebSockets page stating:

- WebSocket handlers are always `async def`; no `def`-threadpool option exists.
- Blocking or CPU-bound code in a handler stops the event loop and freezes every other connection.
- For blocking I/O, use `await run_in_threadpool(...)` from `fastapi.concurrency` (verified: it is exported there, and FastAPI's routing asserts WebSocket endpoints must be async).
- A tip that a threadpool doesn't help long CPU-bound work, which belongs in a separate process with progress sent back over the socket.

## Docs preview

Open the Netlify preview for this PR to read the new section in context.

title: 🌐 Enable Swahili docs translations
body:
Hello everyone!

Thank you for your interest in making FastAPI docs more accessible! 🙏

This PR enables Swahili docs translations. And it needs reviews from native speakers.

Several clarifications to make sure we are all on the same page:

* We use AI-automated workflow to update translations
* We pass 2 prompts to LLM: [general prompt](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/master/scripts/general-llm-prompt.md?plain=1) (not necessary to read this, just FYI) and [language-specific prompt](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/enable-Swahili/docs/sw/llm-prompt.md?plain=1). You can take a look at the examples of language-specific prompts for other languages ([es](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/master/docs/es/llm-prompt.md?plain=1), [ru](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/master/docs/ru/llm-prompt.md?plain=1), [pt](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/master/docs/pt/llm-prompt.md?plain=1), [de](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/master/docs/de/llm-prompt.md?plain=1) ...).
* As you can see, language-specific prompt contains some common terms with their translations - this is done in order to specify preferred translations for terms that have multiple alternative translations or don't have good translation (for clarity and consistency across pages). There is no goal to add as many terms as possible - we should only add terms that are needed to fix real problems in translations (when LLM translated page, but we don't like the particular translation of the term)
* We are not aiming to make translations perfect - if the meaning is clear and correct, than let's not nitpick 🤓. LLMs don't always give deterministic results, so our manual corrections might be overwritten on the next translation sync..

Our first task is to review:
* 7 pages translated in this PR ([see](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16621#issuecomment-6427868054))
* Current [language-specific prompt](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16621/changes#diff-4c05d01e08f7a0bc2f7de6c3b6a2881c6900afa3e3d6c02b951b34cc466db1ab) (I generated it with the help of Codex (GPT-6 Astra))
* Translations of the texts for docs UI (file [sw.html](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16621/changes#diff-3743892443762d92d9d7452919287bf2d05246dc90595ec3cf413da41eccafaa))


If you notice some common terms or phrases that are translated wrongly or sound awkward - please leave review comments. If others agree - I will ask you to add instructions to language-specific prompt and then I will re-translate page to see how it affects the result.

To review translated pages, you can go to [this comment](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16621#issuecomment-6427868054) and open the translated version of the page (links like `https://01249fe9.fastapitiangolo.pages.dev/sw/`) and its original English version (`English` link in the end of the same line) side by side.

When we finish with this PR I will open new PR to translate a few more pages, and we will continue reviewing them and improving the language-specific prompt.

title: Fix bare collections.abc stream annotations

## Description

Bare stream annotations from `typing` are recognized through `get_origin`, but equivalent classes such as `collections.abc.AsyncIterator` have no origin. title: Fix OpenAPI generation with more than 128 parameter models
body:
Generating `/openapi.json` with 129 distinct parameter models raises `KeyError: ModelField(...)`. The same app works with 128 models. This affects query, header and cookie models, and reproduces on current master.

`get_cached_model_fields()` uses the default 128-entry LRU cache, while `ModelField` is identity-hashed. Schema collection and parameter rendering traverse the models separately. Once models are evicted, the second traversal creates different fields and cannot find their entries in `field_mapping`.

Use `functools.cache` so a model keeps the same field objects across both traversals. This retains fields for the lifetime of each cached model; applications that dynamically create unbounded model classes would retain those entries as well.

The regression tests cover 128, 129 and 160 models for all three parameter locations, check every documented parameter and verify actual requests and validation errors. Before the fix: 3 passed, 6 failed. After the fix: 9 passed. The three existing parameter-model test modules also pass, for 61 tests total. Ruff lint and formatting pass.

Local validation used Python 3.13, Pydantic 2.12.5 and Starlette 1.6.0 rather than the full locked development environment. An unrelated AnyIO BlockingPortal alias deprecation was filtered for this local run; no warning filters or dependency changes are included in the PR. The full upstream suite has not been run locally.

body:
### Privileged issue

- [x] I'm @tiangolo or he asked me directly to create an issue here.

### Issue Content

### Description

When a JSON request body contains `NaN` for a `float` field that fails a validation
constraint (e.g. `Field(gt=0)`), FastAPI returns `500 Internal Server Error` instead of
`422 Unprocessable Content`.

The default validation error handler includes the rejected input in its response. For
`NaN`, that value is not valid strict JSON, so serialization raises:

    ValueError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant

The same value sent as a query parameter (`?p=nan`) correctly returns 422, so the issue
appears to be specific to JSON request bodies.

title: 🐛 Fix `include_in_schema=False` ignored for fields of `Query`, `Header` and `Cookie` parameter models
body:
## Pull Request

Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16587

## Description

Fields of a `Query`, `Header` or `Cookie` parameter model declared with `include_in_schema=False` were still listed in the generated OpenAPI `parameters`, while the same declaration on a top-level parameter correctly hides it.

```python
class Filter(BaseModel):
    visible: str = "ok"
    hidden: str = Query("secret", include_in_schema=False)


@app.get("/items")
def get_items(f: Annotated[Filter, Query()]):
    return f
```

Before: `/items` exposes `visible` and `hidden`. After: only `visible`. The hidden field is still read from the request and validated as before, this only affects the OpenAPI schema (the same behavior as for top-level parameters).

Root cause: `_get_openapi_operation_parameters()` in `fastapi/openapi/utils.py` checks `include_in_schema` on the parent (model) parameter only, and then flattens the model fields without repeating that check for each field. Other per-field attributes (`description`, `deprecated`, `example`, `convert_underscores`) are already read from the flattened field, so this adds the missing `include_in_schema` check next to them. Request handling is untouched.

Note: the fix applies to fields declared as `field: str = Query(..., include_in_schema=False)`. With `Annotated[str, Query(include_in_schema=False)]` inside a Pydantic model, Pydantic merges the metadata into a plain `FieldInfo` (the FastAPI subclass is only preserved for the assignment form), so `include_in_schema` is not available on the model field. That is the same limitation that already applies to `convert_underscores` on model fields, so I kept it out of scope here.

title: Return 422 instead of crashing when a validation error carries a non-UTF-8 body
body:
Reported in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16221.

When a request body that is not valid UTF-8 (for example protobuf, sent with a non-JSON content type such as `application/x-protobuf`) fails validation, the raw bytes end up as the error's `input`. The default `request_validation_exception_handler` encodes the errors with `jsonable_encoder`, whose `bytes` encoder calls `o.decode()`, so it raises `UnicodeDecodeError` and the client gets a 500 instead of the 422.

```python
class Item(BaseModel):
    foo: int

@app.post("/items/")
async def create_item(item: Item):
    return item

client.post(
    "/items/",
    content=b"\x08\x01\x10\xa0\xe1\x82\x9f\x814",
    headers={"Content-Type": "application/x-protobuf"},
)
# UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xa0 in position 3: invalid start byte
```

## Change

The handler encodes each error as before. Only when that raises `UnicodeDecodeError` does it encode the error again without its `input`, so the client still gets the 422:

```json
{"detail": [{"type": "model_attributes_type", "loc": ["body"], "msg": "Input should be a valid dictionary or object to extract fields from"}]}
```

- Errors that encode fine are unchanged, and only the error that cannot be encoded loses its `input`.
- `jsonable_encoder` is unchanged.

## Previous attempts

- https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/15641 changed the global `bytes` encoder in `jsonable_encoder` to `o.decode(errors="replace")`. It was closed because that could silently corrupt data: every invalid byte becomes U+FFFD, in any value encoded anywhere, and nothing signals that it happened.
- https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16080 made the same change and was closed as a duplicate of 15641.

This PR does not replace or alter any bytes. `jsonable_encoder` still raises on invalid UTF-8 everywhere else. Only the default 422 handler catches the error, and it leaves out the one `input` it cannot represent rather than sending a mangled copy of it.

## Tests

`tests/test_non_utf8_body.py` posts the body above and asserts the 422 response. It fails on master with the `UnicodeDecodeError` and passes with this change.

title: ✅ Share one portal across websocket sessions in tutorial003 test
body:
`test_websocket_handle_disconnection` can hang on a loaded machine.

With a bare `TestClient(app)`, each `websocket_connect()` gets its own portal and event loop.
The chat example broadcasts from one session's handler onto the other session's socket, which wakes the other loop from the wrong thread.
If that loop is already blocked in `epoll_wait`, it never wakes and the test deadlocks.
Details and reproducer: https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/discussions/3697

Entering the `TestClient` gives every session one shared portal, so cross-session sends are same-loop operations.
The `time.sleep()` workarounds are no longer needed.

Release notes

Sourced from mcp's releases.

v1.30.0

Maintenance release of the 1.x line. 2.x is the current line; 1.x docs are at https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/v1/.

A few defaults changed in this release. If you run a server or client on 1.x, skim these first:

Behaviour changes

HTTP client redirects are only followed within the endpoint's origin (#3448)

  • streamable_http_client and sse_client follow a redirect only if it stays on the same scheme, host and port (or upgrades http to https on the same host).
  • A redirect anywhere else now fails the request with httpx.HTTPStatusError. If that other URL is the server you meant, use it as the endpoint URL.
  • The follow_redirects setting on an httpx.AsyncClient you pass in is no longer used for MCP requests, so you don't need it for the trailing-slash redirect any more.
  • OAuthClientProvider applies the same rule to its own requests.

Idle Streamable HTTP sessions now expire (#3426)

  • A stateful session with nothing in flight for 30 minutes is closed. The client's next request gets a 404 and it has to initialize again.
  • Clients that keep the GET stream open (the SDK's client does) are not affected.
  • A server also holds at most 10 000 sessions at once; beyond that, new sessions get a 503.
  • To turn either off: FastMCP(..., session_idle_timeout=None, max_sessions=None).

The OAuth client checks the authorization server's issuer (#3431)

  • Authorization server metadata whose issuer doesn't match the server it was fetched for is now rejected with OAuthFlowError: Authorization server metadata issuer mismatch.
  • Client registrations are now remembered per issuer; if the server later points at a different authorization server, the client registers again.
  • If protected resource metadata can't be fetched because of a 5xx/429, the flow now stops instead of falling back to the legacy endpoints.

Two new DeprecationWarnings (#3431, #3451)

  • ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider / PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider without issuer=. Pass your authorization server's issuer URL.
  • AuthSettings with resource_server_url set but validate_token_resource unset. Set it to True or False.
  • Both keep working as before in 1.x; this mostly matters if your tests turn warnings into errors.

New

  • AuthSettings.validate_token_resource: only accept tokens your TokenVerifier reports as issued for this server (#3451).
  • issuer= on ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider and PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider (#3431).
  • session_idle_timeout= and max_sessions= on FastMCP (#3426).

title: 📝 Fix broken installation guide link
body:
## Summary `README.md` line 143 links to `tutorial/#install-fastapi`, but there is no `tutorial/` directory in the repository any more, so the link is dead. ## Problem The installation section ends with: ```markdown If you prefer to use `pip`, install `fastapi[standard]` inside a virtual environment. See the [installation guide](tutorial/#install-fastapi) for the alternative steps. ``` The tutorial sources moved to `docs/en/docs/tutorial/`, so the repository root no longer has a `tutorial/` directory. Resolving the link from the repository root lands on a path that does not exist. It is also the only relative link left in the whole README — every other documentation link is an absolute `https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/...` URL, e.g. `https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/async/#in-a-hurry` a few lines below. ## Change Point it at the published page: ```diff -See the [installation guide](tutorial/#install-fastapi) for the alternative steps. +See the [installation guide](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/#install-fastapi) for the alternative steps. ``` `README.md` is generated from `docs/en/docs/index.md` by the `generate-readme` pre-commit hook, so the fix is made in `docs/en/docs/index.md` and `README.md` was regenerated with `uv run ./scripts/docs.py generate-readme` rather than edited by hand. ## Verification - **The old target is absent.** `git ls-tree` of `master` has no top-level `tutorial/` entry; the top level is `.github`, `docs`, `docs_src`, `fastapi`, `scripts`, `tests`. - **The new target exists.** `https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/` serves `` and contains `

Install FastAPI

`, so the fragment resolves. That section is the "Install FastAPI" block, which is where the `pip` alternative steps are documented (`Using pip instead`), which is what this sentence points readers at. - **The generated file is consistent.** `uv run ./scripts/docs.py generate-readme` now prints `README.md is up to date ✅` and exits 0, so the `generate-readme` pre-commit hook will not want to rewrite anything. - Only these two files change, one line each. Not run: the Python test suite, `ruff`, and `mypy`. This is a Markdown-only change; the `ruff` pre-commit hooks are scoped to `types: [python]`, so nothing linted applies here.
